R Markdown source equivalent to `index.html` (the HTML report was computed with `analysis.py`, Python/scikit-learn, because R was not installed on the authoring machine; the numbers in `index.html` come from that run).

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(caret); library(randomForest)
set.seed(1234)
tr <- read.csv("pml-training.csv", na.strings = c("NA", "", "#DIV/0!"))
te <- read.csv("pml-testing.csv",  na.strings = c("NA", "", "#DIV/0!"))
```

```{r clean}
keep <- colMeans(is.na(tr)) < 0.05
tr <- tr[, keep]; te <- te[, keep]
tr <- tr[, -(1:7)]; te <- te[, -(1:7)]   # id, user, timestamps, windows
tr$classe <- factor(tr$classe)
```

```{r split}
inTrain <- createDataPartition(tr$classe, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)
training <- tr[inTrain, ]; validation <- tr[-inTrain, ]
```

```{r model, cache=TRUE}
ctrl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5)
rf <- train(classe ~ ., data = training, method = "rf", trControl = ctrl, ntree = 300)
rf
```

```{r oos}
cm <- confusionMatrix(predict(rf, validation), validation$classe)
cm   # out-of-sample accuracy ~ 0.99
```

```{r predict}
predict(rf, te[, names(te) != "problem_id"])
```
